title: Telemetry Prioritization & Runbook: Inference SLI Mapping
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft to: 1) prioritize telemetry for the inference fleet by business impact, 2) propose a small set of canonical SLIs + metric definitions that map to customer-facing outcomes, 3) provide a compact runbook and dashboard hygiene checklist for new services.

Context / why now:
- We have ~30 services contributing inference traffic; dashboards are proliferating and alerts are noisy.
- Product asks: "why did requests slow down for customer X?" Operationally we need a crisp SLI mapping to answer that with trace+metric signals.
- Goal: reduce incident MTTR by 30% for tail-latency and availability issues within 3 months.

How to read this doc (TL;DR):
- Tier telemetry: immediate (Tier 0), important (Tier 1), nice-to-have (Tier 2).
- SLIs focus on latency (p50/p95/p99), availability (success-rate), and correctness signal (model fallback rate / hallucination proxy).
- Tracing conventions to quickly jump from dashboard anomaly to root cause (span naming + key tags).

1) Prioritized telemetry (single-line descriptions)
- Tier 0 (must have / show on service home dashboard):
  - request_success_rate: per-route success rate excluding client errors (5xx/INF-RT), 1m & 5m windows
  - request_latency_ms_{p50,p95,p99}: end-to-end server latency measured at the ingress handler (only server-side).
  - gpu_utilization_pct: GPU util sampled per instance, 1m avg and 5m avg.
  - queue_depth: length of inference request queue per instance/pool
  - key_cache_hit_rate: prefix/KV cache hit rate (to reason about cost & latency regressions)

- Tier 1 (add to per-feature dashboards):
  - rejected_requests_by_policy: count of requests rejected by rate-limiter / token quota
  - fallback_model_invocations: count of automatic fallback to cheaper model variant
  - memory_pressure_pct: process RSS/GPU memory pressure by instance class
  - streaming_chunk_errors: number of broken streaming sessions or aborted streams

- Tier 2 (exploratory / monthly analysis):
  - token_generation_rate: tokens/sec per model-version
  - user_utterance_length_dist: histogram of incoming prompt lengths
  - instruction_following_proxy: eval-based synthetic rate of correct responses (expensive)

2) Canonical SLI definitions (short version, use for SLOs):
- Availability SLI (service-level):
  name: inference_success_rate_5m
  definition: fraction of requests in 5m window with final status in {200,207} and latency < 30s
  target: 99.9% (prod-critical routes)

- Latency SLI (user-perceived):
  name: user_p95_latency_ms
  definition: 95th percentile of request_latency_ms measured at ingress (includes queue + decode time) over 5m windows
  target: p95 < 300ms for low-latency routes, p95 < 2s for batch routes

- Correctness proxy SLI (guardrail):
  name: fallback_rate_1h
  definition: fraction of requests that triggered model fallback within 1h window
  target: < 0.5% for stable workloads

Notes on choosing percentiles: p50 shows baseline, p95 surface user-impacting tail, p99 for paging-oncall / capacity alarms.

3) Tracing conventions (practical, to get from dashboard to code quickly)
- Span naming:
  - ingress.handle_request (root span)
  - runtime.prepare_inputs
  - runtime.kv_cache_lookup
  - runtime.batch_build
  - runtime.model_decode
  - runtime.kv_cache_update
  - egress.stream_response
- Important span tags (add as baggage/fields):
  - service.name: {service-id}
  - route: {api-route} (e.g., /v1/generate)
  - model.name: {family@version} (e.g., llama2-13b-q4)
content_continued_2:
- pool.id: {dedicated-pool-42}
  - request.id: {uuid} (propagate to logs)
- Trace sampling guidance:
  - Always sample all error traces (status >= 500).
  - Adaptive sampling for latency: sample 100% of requests above p95 latency by route, plus reservoir of 20 traces/min for normal traffic.

4) Dashboard hygiene checklist (for service owners)
- Minimal service home dashboard (visible in Console):
  - Traffic panel: RPS, unique-keys (tenancy), 1m/5m ingestion counts
  - Availability panel: success_rate_5m, 5xx/4xx split
  - Latency panel: p50/p95/p99 as heatmap and trend line
  - Resource panel: GPU util, queue depth, pod count autoscale events
  - Tracing jump: single-click link that opens sampled traces filtered by route & time window
- Keep panels focused: no more than 10 top-level charts; deep dives live in a linked "debug" tab.
- Naming: use service-id prefix for metrics and dashboard titles (e.g., inference-encoder-01 / home).

5) Compact incident runbook snippets (for quick copy-paste)
- High tail latency (p95 increased > 2x for 5m):
  1) Check request queue_depth and gpu_util: if queue grows and GPU util ~100% => capacity.
  2) Inspect recent traces (p95 sample) and look for long runtime.model_decode spans.
  3) If fallback_model_invocations increased recently, investigate model variant change or rollout.
  4) Mitigations: scale up pool; enable temporary routing to cheaper model; apply autoscaler overrides.

- Increased 5xx rate (success_rate drop > 0.5% in 5m):
  1) Open the "errors by code" panel to identify error class (OOM / timeouts / invalid-args).
  2) For OOM: check model.variant and memory_pressure_pct; consider fallback to quantized model.
  3) For timeouts: check queue latency vs model.decode time; extend request timeout or add capacity.

- Cache-surge (key_cache_hit_rate drops suddenly):
  1) Check recent deploys / cache key schema changes.
  2) If cache keys changed, rollback or run migration to rehydrate.
  3) Consider temporarily disabling cache invalidation rules.

6) Onboarding checklist for a new service (minimum viable telemetry)
- Instrumentation (code):
  - Emit request_success_rate, request_latency_ms (histogram), request.size_tokens, request.id on root span.
  - Instrument KV cache metrics and batch sizes.

- Dashboards / Alerts:
  - Create service home dashboard with Tier 0 panels.
content_continued_3: - Create alerts: success_rate_5m < target -> page SRE; p99 latency > threshold -> page oncall; queue_depth > threshold -> notify infra.
content_continued_4:
- Ownership: assign one metric owner and one oncall owner; add contact in dashboard metadata.

7) Signals we often miss (open questions / experiments)
- Signal: "semantic degeneration" proxy — hard to measure in prod. Pilot idea: run synthetic evals per-deploy and surface regression trend. (Related: JIRA-INF-2410)
- Signal: cold-start decode latency correlated with first-token-time; do we need separate SLI for first_token_latency?

8) Action items / next steps (who-what-by)
- (Priya) Draft metric-contract PR: add canonical labels for route/model/pool -> due 2026-02-01 -> JIRA-INF-2378 owner.
- (Evan) Implement p95 trace sampling + dashboard jump link prototype -> due 2026-02-10.
- (Marco) Run a 2-week experiment to surface fallback_rate on high-traffic routes and evaluate for SLOs -> due 2026-03-01.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets:
- Bring examples of noisy alerts to review (top 10 noisy alert rules).
- Decide whether to make p95 SLOs default or route-specific at next cadence.
- Confirm with product which routes are "low-latency" vs "batch".

Unresolved questions:
- What is the canonical timeout value for interactive routes? 15s or 30s? Need product input.
- Do we standardize metric suffixes (ms vs seconds) across teams? There are mixed conventions. Proposal: use ms for latency histograms and seconds for SLI targets, with clear conversions in metric-contracts PR.

References and useful links:
- Telemetry strategy confluence (linked above)
- JIRA-INF-2378 (metric-contracts PR)
- Example dashboard: infra/inference/home (internal link)

Quick glossary:
- SLI: service-level indicator (what we measure).
- SLO: service-level objective (target on SLI).
- SLI error budget: allowed violation window per period.

End of draft.
